chunks: And it is narrated from Minhāl al-Qaṣṣāb, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about intercepting sheep, so he said: “Do not intercept, do not buy what has been intercepted, and do not eat from the meat of what has been intercepted.”

key_terms.الْقَصَّابِ: the butcher; an identifying title for the narrator
key_terms.تَلَقِّي: meeting or intercepting traders or goods before arrival at market
key_terms.تُلُقِّيَ: that which has been intercepted or preemptively met
key_terms.مِنْهَالٍ: Minhāl, the named narrator transmitting this report

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about intercepting sellers before they reach the market?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal prohibition regarding intercepting livestock before they reach the market, then further forbids purchasing or consuming what results from that practice. Its significance lies in protecting fairness in commercial dealings and preventing wrongful market advantage.
